metadata.title: Building Operational Access-Consciousness in a Layered Artificial-Life Model — What Global Access Buys, for Whom Reports Have Value, and When Deliberation Pays / Construcción de conciencia de acceso operacional en un modelo de vida artificial por capas — qué compra el acceso global, para quién vale el informe y cuándo compensa deliberar
metadata.description:
Research compendium of the second phase (V2) of a pre-registered artificial-life research programme (~910 seeded runs in 5 pre-registered batches, N = 8–20 independent seeded runs per condition; 25 pre-registered hypotheses with their outcomes tabulated; a public error ledger with 9 caught errors, 5 of them before measurement). V1 built a functional self-model layer by layer and measured its closures (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21655764). V2 audits V1's design flaws (organs without a body; no access bottleneck; benevolent worlds) and then deliberately builds the missing piece: a global-access workshop — a capacity-1 broadcast channel where modules compete and only the winner governs behaviour. No variable in the codebase is named "consciousness"; the operational construct is access (global availability), and the hard problem is explicitly left untouched. In seeded simulation, between-run noise is low and test statistics are large by construction — not comparable to human studies.

Principal pre-registered results: (1) GLOBAL ACCESS BUYS FUNCTION — first time in the programme that a consciousness-related architectural piece improves the organism: selecting a winner beats broadcasting a randomly chosen module (71.1% vs 30.4% sheltered at tide, t=31.1), beats direct wiring (+14.1 pp, t=5.3), and restores viability (0 collapses vs 3/10); re-entry is sensitive to broadcast content (98.0% vs 80.1% dose-matched null, t=25.1); an emitted report predicts future displacement better than observed behaviour itself (error 0.334 vs 0.440, t=8.9 paired) — functional reportability, built from the inside. (2) THE REPORT'S SYMMETRY — the same report is worth its cost to its own emitter and worth nothing delivered to another organism. Internally: emitting the report costs performance (71.1% baseline to 67.0%), and letting the emitter consume its own report recovers the full cost (back to 71.1%; difference from baseline not significant, t=−0.26), while beating a dose-matched null that carries no report content (t=2.64). Externally: three independent negative routes (t=0.41 / t=0.87 / a permuted control that overturned the one apparent rescue). The channel's current is worth something to its carrier; delivered outward, its content adds nothing a generic nudge does not. This extends V1's closure one floor up: there, no one could read you from outside; here, even explicit declaration does not transfer. (3) TIME IS THE MEDIATOR OF DELIBERATION — the workshop's advantage over direct wiring is a perfect monotone of the world's deadline (5 points, −15.3 pp at half deadline to +25.6 pp at double deadline, t=9.8) while measured conflict stays flat (72–76%): parallel vector-mixing never commits to a course and long deadlines punish it; serial selection is slow but committed. The model thereby derives, rather than assumes, why two processing regimes exist — fast-parallel-uncommitted and slow-serial-committed, each owning its temporal regime. Convergence with dual-process theory is claimed as theoretical convergence only, not identity, and nothing here constitutes evidence about humans.

Additional results: the fully-enabled organism is not viable (3/10 population collapses vs 0/10 with capacities off; the cost is a shared behavioural budget) — function is not free; V1's layer-6 metacognition debt settled in its favour (contrast retained 79–95% under probabilistic flash — the internal signal is broadcast only on a random fraction of steps, which rules out a timekeeping confound — t=6.0–8.9); a refuted mediator honestly recorded (conflict, refuted by triangulation D2) and a sweep-saturation instrument error (error #9) caught by the programme's own identical-digits rule. Falsifiability: a delivered report that beat a dose-matched misdirected control would refute finding 2; a deadline sweep in which the workshop's advantage failed to order monotonically would refute finding 3. Seven untested predictions with their concrete experiments are listed in the closing article (cierre-v2.html, also deposited as a standalone PDF). The corpus contains the founding charter and audit, all pre-registrations, results, engines (dependency-free Node.js, digit-for-digit fidelity to V1 verified, fully seeded), raw JSON outputs of ~910 runs, and the synthesis. Corpus documents are written in Spanish; this metadata record is bilingual, and an English preprint is in preparation. This deposit provides a citable, timestamped record of the V2 programme.
